absent: Scheduling algorithms, wakeup paths, migration decisions and balancing logic beyond the routed type layouts.
Lock ordering, acquisition contexts and runtime flag handling for runqueue and clamp updates.
Deadline timer arming, replenishment, throttling recovery and bandwidth accounting behavior.
Full task descriptor contents beyond the truncated first part and cross subsystem invariants.
Concrete configuration values, sizing defaults and entry point implementations not shown in fragments.

findings.text: Prior CPU time record keeps separate user and system totals guarded by a raw spin primitive, with the whole record omitted when native virtual accounting is enabled.
Virtual time mode has five ordered conditions covering inactive, idle, kernel execution, user execution and guest execution, with inactive as the zero value.
Virtual time accounting record combines sequence protection with a start timestamp, a mode value, a CPU identifier and three cumulative counters for user, system and guest time.
Utilization clamp index distinguishes minimum and maximum, with minimum at zero and a trailing count that sizes per task clamp arrays.
Scheduling parameter block carries a single integer priority.
Scheduling info block, present only when info accounting is configured, accumulates run count plus waiting time totals with observed extremes and keeps arrival, queueing and peak waiting timestamps.
Fixed point shift is ten and the corresponding scale is one shifted left by that amount.
Capacity shift equals the fixed point shift and capacity scale is one shifted left by the capacity shift.
Load weight record pairs an absolute weight with a cached reciprocal that lets the scheduler use multiplication rather than division.

Per entity average tracking keeps last update time, decaying sums for load, runnable and utilization, a period contribution, and derived averages including an estimated utilization, placed on its own cache line.
Estimation weight shift is two and the unchanged marker is the high bit of a thirty two bit word.

Statistics block, present only when scheduler statistics are configured, tracks waiting, input output waiting, sleeping and blocking intervals with counts and extremes, execution extremes, migration failure and forced migration counts, and a breakdown of wakeup kinds including synchronous, migrating, local, remote and affine attempts, plus a core idle total when core scheduling is configured, placed on its own cache line.

Fair scheduling entity links load weight values, a tree node, deadline and virtual time markers, protected deadline and slice state, queue membership flags, execution accounting, migration count, optional group hierarchy pointers with depth and runnable weight, and an embedded average record held apart to avoid cache collision.

Realtime scheduling entity links a run list node, timeout and watchdog stamps, a remaining slice, queue membership indicators, a back pointer and optional group hierarchy pointers, with randomized layout.
Deadline server picker is a function pointer type that selects a task from a deadline entity while runqueue flags are held.

Deadline entity stores configured runtime, deadline, period and two derived densities, plus live remaining runtime, absolute deadline and behavior flags, eleven single bit conditions for throttling, yielding, non contending, overrun, server roles and defer states, two high resolution timers for enforcement and inactivity, a runqueue link with picker callback, and an optional inheritance donor pointer.
Bucket count is taken from the configured bucket count option.
Clamp entry packs a value sized to represent the capacity scale, a bucket identifier sized to represent the bucket count, and single bit active and user defined markers.
Read copy update special state is a union offering either four byte fields for blocked, quiescent need, expedite hint and barrier need, or a single thirty two bit word view of the same storage.
Performance task context index uses negative one for invalid, zero for hardware, next for software and a trailing count.
Total performance context count is four.
Wake queue node is a singly linked element holding only a next pointer.
Local mapping control is empty unless local mapping is configured, in which case it holds an index plus saved page table entries sized by the maximum index.
Inter processor interrupt mask has two exclusive shapes, either a union of a mask pointer and an inline value or an empty record, selected by configuration.

Task descriptor prefix carries execution state with a saved copy for lock sleepers, stack, reference count, flags, wakeup linkage with flip history and affinity hints, three priority levels plus realtime priority, embedded fair, realtime and deadline entities with server link and class pointer, core scheduling node when configured, group membership with throttling state, requested and effective clamp arrays sized by the clamp count, statistics, notifier list when configured, policy, capacity limit, allowed CPU bookkeeping with pointers, mask and migration control.

Visible descriptor remainder carries read copy update tracking, scheduling info, runqueue and tree linkage, memory pointers, execution identity, exit and signal state, credentials, naming, filesystem, file, namespace and accounting members, plus CPU time totals with scaled variants when configured, guest time, prior time and virtual time records, tick dependency, switch counts, start stamps and fault counts.

Prior time totals are serialized by their embedded raw primitive, clamp arrays require runqueue lock held, scheduler control bits require scheduler locks, and the descriptor provides separate allocation, inheritance and blocking primitives with documented protection for memory, credential and signaling members.

When thread info lives in the task it must be first, clamp arrays are sized by the clamp count, fair entity average is isolated on its own line, statistics and average records request cache alignment, realtime entity requests randomized layout, and the descriptor marks the start of its randomizable region after scheduling critical members.

Remote wakeup flag is stored outside the scheduler word and relies on an explicit barrier pairing between deactivation and queueing, the read copy update special union and the interrupt mask union alias the same storage under different views, and empty versus non empty shapes for mapping control and interrupt mask change member presence by configuration so generic access must respect the active configuration.
Maximum lock depth tracked per task is forty eight.
